summary: Phase 136AC independently re-derived and verified the Phase 136AB AuthorityEpoch/AuthorityState typed record models against the frozen executable schemas directly (records/authority_epoch.schema.json, records/authority_state.schema.json), via a new independent test module (tests/test_cltr_authority_136ac_authority_core_independent.py, 104 tests, all passing, 1 skipped) that imports nothing from 136AB's own test module. Verified exact field/discriminator/enum/identifier/digest/reference-family conformance, absent-vs-null distinctions and every conditional branch (activation_state<->generation_binding, authority_kind<->authoritative_generation, verification_state<->uncertainty), non-resolving references (instrumented filesystem/socket probes), exact timestamp wire-string preservation (no Z<->+00:00 normalization, no clock read), lossless round trip, recursive immutability, structural equality, zero forbidden operational-authority methods (AST-verified), zero cross-record semantic validation (schema-valid-but-fabricated records construct successfully), zero later-group models (AST-verified, and the 136M scope guard confirmed correctly narrowed to the 14 later-group names only), zero production runtime imports (both directions), zero side effects (subprocess/socket/env/write-open/hashlib.sha256 all instrumented), and a fresh wheel/sdist with isolated installed-wheel construction outside the repository checkout. One NON-BLOCKING finding disclosed, not repaired: CONFIRMED-136AC-1 -- all four EnumClass(raw_str) construction call sites (activation_state, authority_kind, verification_state, compatibility_mode, and transitively authority_role) raise a bare stdlib ValueError rather than a TypedModelError subclass on rejection; the rejection itself is correctly fail-closed (no coercion, no silent acceptance), only the exception type is inconsistent with the module's own documented error hierarchy; 136AB's own focused test suite already baked this in as expected behavior via pytest.raises(ValueError) rather than disclosing it. Fresh regression: 514 passed (new suite + 136AB/136AA/136Z reruns); bounded Authority-Core-adjacent sweep (cltr_authority + cltr_cutover_136* + canonicalization + digest + models + validation + schema_runtime + runtime_registry) 3220 passed/9 skipped/1 failed (identical inherited 136U scope-guard gap already disclosed by 136AA, unrelated -- enums.py untouched since Phase 136Z); test_cltr_135o_integration.py + test_cltr_migration_135p_verification.py 21 passed/8 failed (identical pre-existing, unrelated cluster); Fast Green 4391 passed (unchanged baseline). Zero new failures anywhere. No later record-family model, semantic validator, repository, persistence, resolver, or runtime integration was implemented or repaired in this phase. Legacy lifecycle remains the sole production authority; CLTR remains derivative; runtime remains Observed / observe / execution unavailable. Verdict: AUTHORITY CORE VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- READY FOR REQUEST AND READINESS MODEL IMPLEMENTATION.
